candidate_sentence_map.S1: Coop Pank delivered strong business growth in 2025, although profitability declined as falling interest rates reduced margins.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: Net profit was €28.7 million, down 11% from €32.2 million in 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: Profit before tax decreased to €34.6 million from €36.7 million, while return on equity fell from 16.2% to 12.9% and return on assets from 1.6% to 1.2%.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: Net interest income declined 6% to €73.3 million, and net interest margin narrowed from 3.8% to 3.0%.
candidate_sentence_map.S5: This reflected the lower-interest-rate environment, which was not fully offset by the 19% expansion in business volumes.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: Net fee and commission income increased 4% to €4.5 million, while net other income improved to €1.5 million from approximately zero in 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S7: Operating expenses rose 2% to €41.5 million, resulting in a higher cost-to-income ratio of 52.3%, compared with 49.6% a year earlier.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: Credit loss allowance decreased to €3.3 million from €4.6 million, and management reported that portfolio quality remained at a low-risk level, with low overdue debt and limited demand for payment holidays.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: Income tax expense increased to €5.8 million from €4.5 million, with the effective tax rate rising from 12% to 17%.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: The bank’s loan portfolio grew by €340 million, or 19%, to €2.11 billion, exceeding €2 billion for the first time.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: Business lending increased 27%, or €207 million, and the home-loan portfolio rose 17%, or €125 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: Customer deposits increased 9% to €2.05 billion, with demand deposits up 11% and term deposits up 8%.
candidate_sentence_map.S13: The customer base expanded by 19,000, or 9%, to 227,000.
candidate_sentence_map.S14: Total assets increased to €2.70 billion from €2.19 billion, while shareholders’ equity rose to €234.5 million from €211.6 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: Performance benefited from the beginning of Estonia’s economic recovery, stronger loan demand and greater investment activity.
candidate_sentence_map.S16: Estonia’s GDP grew 0.7% in 2025, while declining inflation and interest rates supported confidence among businesses and households.
candidate_sentence_map.S17: However, the six-month Euribor fell to 2.1% by year-end, contributing to pressure on interest income.
candidate_sentence_map.S18: Coop Pank diversified funding by issuing €250 million of four-year covered bonds, the first tranche of a €750 million programme.
candidate_sentence_map.S19: It also signed an EIB Group guarantee agreement enabling up to €249 million of new business lending; the transaction had not become effective and had no impact on 2025 results.
candidate_sentence_map.S20: Moody’s affirmed the bank’s Baa2 deposit rating with a positive outlook.
candidate_sentence_map.S21: Capital requirements were met, although the CET1 ratio declined to 14.15% from 14.28% and total capital adequacy to 18.54% from 19.41%.
candidate_sentence_map.S22: The bank paid €7.2 million in dividends for 2024 and proposed a €0.065-per-share dividend from 2025 profit.

evaluation.label: Generally yes
evaluation.justification: All HIGH-importance items are fully covered except K6, which is only partially covered (the guarantee agreement is mentioned but the core purpose of transferring credit risk and enabling new loans is omitted). The MEDIUM item K7 is entirely missing. K8 is fully represented. Overall, the main picture of 2025 performance and growth is captured with only two material omissions.
